clue.text: Form of Scotch some prefer, habitually drunk around clubs

indicators.note: around says the drunkard's word is wrapped about the clubs letter

parts.note: sottish describes a sot, someone who is habitually drunk
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A whisky drinker who is always tipsy orders a preferred form of Scotch while doing the rounds of the clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Many people prefer to call things from Scotland 'Scottish', keeping 'Scotch' for whisky; here it also names the Scottish Play, the theatre's euphemism for the play this whole puzzle draws on.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for things from Scotland is often preferred to the older variant used mainly for whisky.

clue.text: Damned dog dismissed in tragic scene?

definitions.text: Damned dog dismissed in tragic scene?

parts.words: Damned dog dismissed in tragic scene?
parts.note: Lady Macbeth cries 'Out, damned ...!' in the sleepwalking scene, and a traditional name for a dog is the same word

explanation.surface: A cursed hound is driven out during a tragic moment on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'damned dog' is the stain Lady Macbeth tries to wash off; 'dismissed' echoes her command 'Out!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic pet dog's name matches the bloodstain Lady Macbeth orders away in her famous sleepwalking line.

clue.text: For example, removed branches over soldiers

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
men are ordinary soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Troops are shown cut-down boughs held above them, as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth the soldiers cut branches from Birnam Wood to hide their numbers, fulfilling the prophecy that the wood would come to Dunsinane: an example of a portent.
explanation.definitionFit: The moving wood was a portent, a sign foretold by the witches that Macbeth's doom was near.

clue.text: Old landed gentry, some with an estate

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Aristocrats of the past, a few of whom owned country property.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth himself is Thane of Glamis and Cawdor, which ties this to the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanes were Anglo-Saxon and Scottish noblemen holding land from the king, an old landed rank.

clue.text: As guilty woman dramatically did, walked out

definitions.meaning: Lady Macbeth, guilty of the king's murder, sleepwalks in the play
walked while out cold, that is, walked in one's sleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Walked out' looks like leaving in protest; 'out' here means unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking while asleep is what Lady Macbeth does on stage in her guilty night wanderings.

clue.text: Like late guest king saw at banquet, in spot occupied by none, right?

definitions.text: Like late guest king saw at banquet

indicators.note: occupied by says the spotting verb is filled with the other pieces

parts.note: to spot something is to spy it
O is zero, none
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A ghostly visitor seen by a king at a feast sits in a seat that nobody has taken, correct?
explanation.walkthrough: The late guest is Banquo's ghost, which Macbeth alone sees sitting in his empty place at the banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is eerie and spectral, which is the adjective's sense here.

clue.text: Under pressure, atoning can become emotionally painful

indicators.note: in a down entry the rearranged word sits under the pressure letter, which comes first

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

indicators.note: can become says the letters of atoning turn into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Making amends while under strain can turn out to be heart-rending.
explanation.definitionFit: Something poignant moves one to sorrow, so it is painful in a deeply felt way.

clue.text: Totally lacking old engraving tool that's no longer fashionable

parts.note: being out of something means having none of it left
a style is an old word for a stylus, a pointed tool for marking wax or metal

explanation.surface: Without a traditional etcher's implement, which has gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing past its vogue is said to be dated, no longer in the current mode.

clue.text: Indeed, strayed badly — all of which enlightened fools?

parts.note: yes affirms, like indeed

indicators.note: badly says the letters of strayed are put in a poor, jumbled order

explanation.surface: Someone admits that they went badly astray, the way past days lit the way for fools.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth's 'Tomorrow' speech says 'all our yesterdays have lighted fools the way to dusty death'.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth's soliloquy says past days have lighted fools on their way to death.

clue.text: Warmly welcoming new layout for promenade

indicators.note: a new layout means the letters of promenade are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A friendly-looking redesign of a seaside walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: Greeting someone with outstretched limbs ready to embrace means receiving them warmly.

clue.text: Advice to players about 1 across 19? You're welcome!

definitions.meaning: actors are superstitiously warned never to name Macbeth, the Scottish Play, in a theatre
a polite reply to thanks, brushing the favour aside

explanation.walkthrough: 1 across 19 means SCOTTISH PLAY, the euphemism actors use to avoid saying the play's real title.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase both warns actors not to name the cursed play and politely waves away someone's thanks.

clue.text: Kind of stress that's central to conflict, usually

indicators.note: central to says the letters sit in the middle of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A type of tension that typically lies at the heart of a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody this term names the rhythmical stress falling on a syllable in a line of verse.

clue.text: Cost of brief engagement?

parts.note: a brief is a barrister, and engaging one in advance costs an upfront payment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief engagement' suggests a short betrothal; a brief is slang for a barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment made to secure a lawyer's services in advance is the price of hiring counsel.

clue.text: Blonde isn't stupid, or totally lacking in vision

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters of the two words are muddled

explanation.surface: A fair-haired person is not dim, nor unable to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pokes at the 'dumb blonde' stereotype; 'stupid' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound means completely sightless, an intensified form of being without sight.

clue.text: As play is shown again, perhaps, creeps in this petty pace?

definitions.text: As play is shown again, perhaps
definitions.meaning: television replays of sports action are often shown at reduced speed
Macbeth's line 'Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow, creeps in this petty pace' describes time crawling

explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' suggests a drama; here it is a piece of sporting action replayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay at reduced speed crawls along, just as time creeps at a petty pace in Macbeth's speech.

clue.text: 24's narrative to follow in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A fool's story to be tracked in a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is IDIOT: life is 'a tale told by an idiot' in Macbeth's speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A story or narrative is what Macbeth says life is, told by a fool.

clue.text: A bishop held top position, having deposed leader that's detested

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: deposed leader says the first letter of the dominating word is removed

parts.note: to dominate is to hold the top position

explanation.surface: A churchman who was in charge, then ousted his chief, is loathed.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe, so something abominated is hated intensely.

clue.text: Check with reserve force, containing extreme feud

indicators.note: containing says the checking word and reserve force hold the extremity inside

parts.note: to vet is to check
an end is an extremity
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: An inspection alongside volunteer troops, holding back a bitter quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged blood feud between families, as in Macbeth's revenge cycle.

clue.text: Stronghold of rugby three-quarters, so to speak — with passion as well

parts.note: three of the four compass quarters are north, east and west, abbreviated N, E, W
zeal is passion or fervour
and means as well

explanation.surface: A rugby powerhouse whose backs play with fervour too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three-quarters' are rugby backs, but here they are compass points: the four quarters are N, S, E, W.
explanation.definitionFit: The All Blacks' homeland is famed for rugby, the country's national sport.

clue.text: Act as beginner in party, unlike minister

indicators.note: the beginner in a word is its opening letter

parts.note: lay means not of the clergy, unlike a minister

explanation.surface: Behave like a novice at a celebration, not like a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginner' wants to be L for learner; it is the first letter of 'party'.
explanation.definitionFit: To act a part on stage is to perform it, a synonym in the theatrical sense.

clue.text: Cutting male player with peripheral role

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a wing plays out on the flank in football or rugby

explanation.surface: Dropping a man who plays on the fringes of the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewing means chopping with an axe, a form of cutting.

clue.text: How lady saw her hand, after partner disposed of king

definitions.text: How lady saw her hand, after partner disposed of king

parts.words: How lady saw her hand, after partner disposed of king
parts.note: after her husband murders King Duncan, Lady Macbeth sees blood on her hand that will not wash off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' and 'partner' suggest a card game such as bridge, but the lady is Lady Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered with blood marks is how Lady Macbeth sees her hand in the sleepwalking scene.

clue.text: Weird trio played — is entertaining around midnight

indicators.note: around says the entertaining word goes round the midnight letter

parts.note: to have an idea is to entertain it, so has means is entertaining
the middle letter of night is G

explanation.surface: Three strange figures in a performance welcome guests at the stroke of twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: The weird sisters, the witches of Macbeth, are the trio in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The three witches are ugly old crones, so the word for such women fits.

clue.text: Supposedly heavy drinker, partly blinded for a spell?

definitions.meaning: British slang says a drunk person is 'pissed as a ...'
the witches' brew needs 'eye of ...', so a ... that gave one up is partly blind

explanation.walkthrough: 'For a spell' looks like 'for a while'; it means for a magic charm.
explanation.definitionFit: This amphibian is proverbially drunk, and its eye goes into the witches' cauldron in Macbeth.

clue.text: Crazy source of loud and furious, but meaningless, story

definitions.text: Crazy source of loud and furious, but meaningless, story

parts.words: Crazy source of loud and furious, but meaningless, story
parts.note: Macbeth calls life a tale told by a fool, full of sound and fury, signifying nothing

explanation.surface: A madman telling a noisy, angry tale that means nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or simpleton is the teller of the meaningless tale in Macbeth's soliloquy.

clue.text: Horses in front of empty castle

indicators.note: in front of places the horses before the emptiness word

parts.note: duns are greyish-brown horses
inane means empty or senseless

explanation.surface: Horses stand before a deserted fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: The castle is Macbeth's stronghold, to which Birnam Wood comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth's fortress in the play is this Scottish hill castle.

clue.text: Surprisingly full-blooded 1 across king

parts.note: Lady Macbeth asks who would have thought the old man to have had so much blood in him, of the murdered Scots ruler

explanation.surface: A Scots monarch unexpectedly full of blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is SCOTTISH; the line comes from Lady Macbeth's sleepwalking scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The murdered Scottish monarch in Macbeth astonishes Lady Macbeth with how much blood he had.

clue.text: Get seats rearranged where actors perform

indicators.note: rearranged says the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Move the chairs about in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage set is the built scenery on the boards where a play is acted.
